findings.ac: Stress: corrupted/missing references/ files detected by setup/update
findings.text: skill_problems() only detects a cited reference that is absent (is_file() false); an empty, truncated or non-UTF-8 references/*.md passes (non-UTF-8 would raise an uncaught UnicodeDecodeError instead of a report). test_suite_detects_missing_reference_file only unlinks refs[0], so no assertion covers the 'corrupted' half of the AC, nor a transitively cited or absolute-form (.agents/skills/x/references/) citation.

Every suite test passes --skills-dir explicitly; the default path the SKILL.md relies on ('no argument needed', PLUGIN_ROOT.parent in cmd_suite) is never exercised, so a regression in default skills-dir resolution would not fail any test.

findings.ac: setup/update halt (non-fatal halt, do not scaffold / HALT without touching the project)
findings.text: The wiring tests (test_setup_runs_suite_check_before_scaffolding..., test_update_runs_suite_and_legacy_checks_before_scope...) assert only str.index ordering of 'check_suite.py suite/legacy/visibility' vs scaffold.py / Phase 1 / Checkpoint 9 / Phase 6. Nothing asserts the halt instructions ('do **not** scaffold', '**HALT** without touching the project', print report verbatim), so deleting them would still pass.

findings.ac: System pack in .agents/skills but absent from Claude dir -> halts, lists, copy/sync remediation
findings.text: test_claude_host_halts_when_system_pack_only_in_agents_skills checks only names, the trivially true substrings '.claude' and 'skills', and the presence of 'Copy-Item' and 'cp -r'; it never asserts the actual source (.agents/skills/<name>) or destination (project .claude/skills/<name>) in the copy commands, and the mixed case (one skill on disk elsewhere, one absent -> cp plus /sync-skills together) and the home-level source are untested.
